objective.value: Determine how rapidly a large-scale fire grows in low gravity, and investigate low-gravity flammability limits compared with NASA's normal-gravity material flammability screening test.

sources.note: PSI-98 'objective': (1) determine how rapidly a large-scale fire grows in low gravity and (2) investigate the low-g flammability limits vs those from NASA's normal-gravity material flammability screening test.
PSI-98 'researchImpacts': results determine microgravity flammability limits and help validate NASA's material selection criteria (prevention via material selection).
Challenge brief, Background: Saffire-I/-II/-III are flammability studies of solid materials (fabrics, plastics) that inform prevention via material selection.

safety_functions.note: PSI ties the results to flammability limits and material selection criteria (prevention); the brief groups Saffire under prevention/material selection. The PSI proposal title mentions improved fire detection, but the flown Saffire-I experiment is a flame-spread/flammability study.

sources.note: PSI-98 'approach': two cameras; thermocouples for flow, flame and plume temperature; two radiometers for flame radiation; solid-state sensors for pressure, CO2 and O2 mole fraction; two anemometers for flow velocity.
PSI-98 'researchImpacts': instruments on the uncrewed cargo vessel measure oxygen, carbon dioxide, heat, pressure and flame growth; two video cameras view the flame.

relevance_notes.value: Cited in the brief as a solid-material flammability study for prevention and material selection. Saffire-I burned a single large (0.94 m) fabric sample in microgravity at ~21.5% O2 to measure how fast a large fire grows and to set low-gravity flammability limits against NASA's normal-gravity screening test, at a scale far larger than earlier ISS flame-spread experiments.

sources.note: PSI-98 'objective' and 'approach': large-scale fire growth and low-g flammability limits using a ~0.94 m fabric sample in microgravity.
Challenge brief, Background: Saffire-I/-II/-III are flammability studies of solid materials (fabrics, plastics) that inform prevention via material selection.

value: Fire safety and prevention in small sealed environments such as mines, airplanes and submarines
Validation of material flammability selection and screening criteria

sources.note: PSI-98 'researchImpacts': results help validate NASA's material selection criteria; studying fire in small sealed environments such as the Cygnus cargo vehicle benefits fire safety and prevention on Earth, including inside mines, airplanes or submarines.

conditions.pressure_psi is unknown: the PSI-98 experimental table has no pressure column and no source read gives a pressure value (the PSI approach mentions a pressure sensor but no number).
Only two test rows exist in the PSI-98 experimental table (sample S1 concurrent, sample S2 opposed); the F1C1/F1C2 and F2C1/F2C2 rows are pre-test flow-visualisation data with no conditions.
The sample size is stated two ways: the approach text says ~0.94 m long x 0.4 m wide, while the table lists sample length 40.6 cm and width 94 cm (same card, axes transposed).
